diagram_math_checks.result: Both left nodes are Ind_H^G 1_H; both right nodes are C^(G/H). The horizontal Phi is the linear bijection of proof step 2.1. L_x is an endomorphism of the induced module by the full local induced-module definition, since (L_x f)(gh)=f(x^{-1}gh)=f(x^{-1}g). P_x is an endomorphism of functions on left cosets because x^{-1}(gh)H=x^{-1}gH.

def-coset defines left cosets as gH={gh:h in H}. The trivial action makes f(gh)=f(g) by step 1.1. Hence Phi(f)(gH)=f(g) is representative independent. Pullback q*F=F composed with q, q(g)=gH, is inverse on both sides; G finite means all functions on G/H identify with the free permutation module.

For every x,g in G and induced f, (Phi L_x f)(gH)=f(x^{-1}g)=(P_x Phi f)(gH), exactly proof step 3.1 and the supplier left-action formula. All four arrows have their displayed source/target; square expresses P_x composed with Phi = Phi composed with L_x.

Phi(1_{gH}) is delta at the coset gH because left cosets are equal or disjoint; inverse image under q of that singleton is the subset gH. L_x(1_{gH})(a)=1 precisely when x^{-1}a belongs to gH, equivalently a belongs to xgH. Thus L_x 1_{gH}=1_{xgH}; the supplier permutation formula gives P_x e_{gH}=e_{xgH}. No representative choice, double cosets or tensor balancing is used.
All four original proof steps are byte-for-byte preserved and establish the result before Remarks; the diagram merely displays step 3.1.
